question_text: Mention the differences between virulent phages and temperate phages.

insider_note: One cycle against two. That is the difference, and each half needs its named example.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Virulent phages
steps.margin_note: One cycle, the outcome, one example. Four lines.
lines: VIRULENT PHAGES replicate only through the LYTIC
They always destroy the host cell.
Example: the T-even phages (T2, T4, T6).
steps.why: A phage with only one cycle available has no way to wait, so it must kill the host every time.
common_mistakes: Saying virulent phages can go lysogenic. They cannot; only the lytic cycle is open to them.
Naming no example. The T-even phages are the standard one.
steps.memory_tip: Only one cycle, so the host always dies.

steps.label: Temperate phages
steps.margin_note: Both cycles, what lysogeny does, one example. The word lysogenic is the mark.

lines.text: Virulent phages have one cycle; temperate

lines: TEMPERATE PHAGES replicate through BOTH the lytic
In the lysogenic cycle the phage DNA joins the
bacterial chromosome and is copied with it, so
steps.why: Joining the host chromosome lets the phage be copied for generations without killing anything, so it can wait for better conditions before turning lytic.
common_mistakes: Saying temperate phages never lyse the host. They CAN — they have both cycles.
Naming a T-even phage. Coliphage lambda is the temperate example.
